rules.note: Greek θ is т in borrowings that came through Western Europe.
Greek θ is ф in the older borrowings that came through Byzantium and the Church.
Greek and Latin h usually becomes г.
Sometimes the h is simply dropped.
Latin x is spelled out as кс.

rules.pattern: c → ц before e, i, y
rules.note: Latin c before a front vowel is ц; before a, o, u it is к.
An initial e is spelled э, keeping it from being read as ye.
A science in -ics is -ика, feminine singular.
Greek -μα gives -ма, feminine in Russian though neuter in Greek.
Latin -alis takes the Russian adjective ending: -альный.
Any borrowed stem becomes an adjective with -н-ый.
Greek -ος, -ον and Latin -us, -um are usually dropped.
